name: POST /api/leadflow/contacts/:id/resolve - ask upstream which canonical person this contact is
description:
Sends the contact's name, email and phone to sdk-identity-resolver and answers which canonical person they identify. An ACTION on an existing record, so 200 rather than 201 (MUST-54) - nothing is created here that the caller names.

WHY THE ENDPOINT EXISTS. Every governed screen reading ProjexCloud names its subject by canonical person id: the consent register names the subject of a receipt that way, Identity Review names both sides of a candidate link that way. LeadFlow held no such key, so both screens rendered raw uuids at a Privacy Officer and at a Data Steward - the two roles least able to act on one. This is where leads.canonical_person_id comes from.

ONLY AN EXACT CROSSWALK IS RECORDED, and the asymmetry is the point rather than an implementation detail. match_type 'exact_crosswalk' means a recorded identifier - an app_identity or an alias hash held WITHIN this tenant - already names that person, so the id is written to the lead and returned with recorded:true. 'possibly_same' is a guess: a candidate link has been raised upstream for steward review and review_case_id carries it, but NOTHING is written here, because a name shown on a consent receipt on the strength of a guess is the most expensive mistake this product can make. 'no_match' writes nothing either.

IDEMPOTENT BY OUTCOME. Re-running against a contact already carrying the id answers the same match_type with recorded:false - the id was already there, so no row changed. A caller cannot tell that apart from a failure unless the response says so, which is why `recorded` is separate from `canonical_person_id`.

AN UNREACHABLE RESOLVER IS 503, NEVER 'no_match' (the single most important negative here). Reporting an outage as "this person is new" is precisely how a duplicate identity gets created, and the caller has to be able to tell the two apart to decide whether to retry.

Edge cases: a contact with no name, email or phone answers 422 - there is no bundle to resolve and answering no_match would report an absence nobody looked for; a contact id that does not exist answers 404 before any upstream call is made. QA: measured live against a real contact from the list.

testCases.name: Resolving a contact answers with a match type and an account of the decision
Re-resolving the same contact is a no-op rather than a second write
NEGATIVE: no contact with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.when: the contact id does not exist. Checked before any upstream call, so an unknown id never raises a candidate link.

errorCases.message: This contact carries no name, email or phone, so there is nothing to resolve it by
errorCases.when: every trait the matcher scores on is absent. 422 rather than 400: the request is well-formed and the refusal is about the record's contents.

errorCases.message: The identity resolver could not be reached, so this contact is unresolved rather than new
errorCases.when: sdk-identity-resolver is unreachable or the circuit is open. Deliberately NOT reported as no_match - an outage read as 'this person is new' is how a duplicate identity gets created.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
